result.title: Can Vision-Language Models Truly Understand Images? A Benchmark Beyond Commonsense Bias
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance on a wide range of vision-language tasks. However, it remains unclear whether their predictions are grounded in the visual content itself or are largely driven by statistical co-occurrence patterns and commonsense correlations learned from large-scale image-text corpora. Existing vision-language benchmarks predominantly consist of samples that conform to human commonsense, allowing models to achieve strong performance by exploiting dataset priors rather than genuinely understanding image content. To address this limitation, we present ContraSense, a systematically constructed benchmark for evaluating faithful vision-language understanding. ContraSense consists of carefully curated counter-intuitive image-text pairs that deliberately violate common expectations, substantially reducing the effectiveness of statistical biases and requiring models to rely on visual evidence for reasoning. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on a diverse set of representative open- and closed-source MLLMs. The results reveal a substantial performance gap between current MLLMs and humans: even the strongest closed-source model achieves only about 60\% accuracy, compared with 96.04\% for human participants. These findings demonstrate that current MLLMs still struggle with faithful visual understanding and highlight the need for more robust multimodal reasoning grounded in image content. The ContraSense benchmark is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/LingLin00/ContraSense.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 ContraSense 基准，用违背常识的图像-文本对削弱统计先验，评测多种开源与闭源 MLLM 是否真正依赖视觉证据作答，并报告最强闭源模型约 60% 准确率、远低于人类的 96%。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接检验 VLM 是否因语言先验而绕过视觉内容，可作为核查 LVR 中视觉旁路与信息坍缩代价、以及 latent 状态是否保留任务必要视觉细节的评测参照。
